title: Adjoining p-th roots of p-independent elements gives degree p^n
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $a_1,\dots,a_n\in k$ be elements such that $\mathrm da_1,\dots,\mathrm da_n$ are linearly independent over $k$ in the module of K\"ahler differentials $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $\bar k$ be an algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $a_i^{1/p}\in\bar k$ the (unique) $p$-th roots. Then the subfield $k(a_1^{1/p},\dots,a_n^{1/p})\subseteq\bar k$, the smallest subfield containing $k$ and the $a_i^{1/p}$, is a finite extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] of degree $p^n$ (its dimension as a $k$-vector space).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07DZ (lemma-size-extension-pth-roots, line 44229) and its proof (induction on n, the case n = 1 being Lemma Tag 031W, lemma-derivative-zero-pth-power, line 44174); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Induct on n, retaining the claim that the field generated by the n given roots is finite over k and has finrank p^n. For n=0 the generating range is empty, the adjunction is bottom, and IntermediateField.finrank_bot gives degree one. Restrict differential independence to Fin.castSucc for the induction hypothesis.

For the successor case let L be the preceding root field. Apply pth_root_not_mem_previous_adjoin to obtain alpha_last not in L. This is precisely the differential obstruction from steps 2 and 3 of the previous plan; it states neither finite dimensionality nor the degree formula.

Put b = a_last viewed in L. If c^p=b in L, mapping to Omega and injectivity of Frobenius would identify c with alpha_last, contrary to its nonmembership. Hence X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_prime (the existing 09HF Mathlib leaf) proves X^p-C(b) irreducible. It is monic and annihilates alpha_last. minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic identifies it with the minimal polynomial, while the same explicit polynomial proves integrality. IntermediateField.adjoin.finiteDimensional and adjoin.finrank, the finite-dimensional and degree consequences of the simple-extension power basis, give finite dimensionality over L and degree p.

Module.Finite.trans and Module.finrank_mul_finrank give finiteness over k and degree p^n*p=p^(n+1). The range of the successor family is the union of the preceding range and the singleton last root. IntermediateField.adjoin_adjoin_left identifies the iterated adjunction, after restricting scalars, with the required field.

The lead's suggested route via the p-th-root presentation of differentials is not the source's and is not used. Statement: algebraic closure and finite-extension notions now cited; content unchanged.
